Glucose = loose coins you spend on the spot.

board_events.text: The formula is a HINT, not a definition.
Glucose $C_6H_{12}O_6$ fits as $C_6(H_2O)_6$ — a coincidence.

segments.text: <curious>Why does the body juggle so many different sugars at once?</curious> Picture a busy Saturday market in Pune. To understand every carbohydrate, you only need one image: how money moves through that market.
Glucose is the loose change. It is the small-change currency that every single cell can spend on the spot for instant energy, with no delay.

At day's end the vendor bundles the takings into a thick wad and locks it in an almirah. That is starch in plants and glycogen in animals: energy folded into a storable form, broken back into coins only when needed.
The wooden shelf and the cotton kurta are cellulose: sugar units chained together not for energy but purely for structure. Same bricks, a completely different job.
Hold this one picture in your head: coins to spend, a locked wad to store, a shelf for structure. Spend, store, structure captures almost the whole chapter in a single frame.

Chemically, carbohydrates are optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones, or compounds that yield such units on hydrolysis. The old name came from this general formula, because they looked like hydrates of carbon.

But treat that formula as a loose historical hint, never a definition. Acetic acid fits the same pattern yet is no sugar, and rhamnose is a genuine sugar that does not fit. Always lean on the functional-group definition instead.
Glucose does fit neatly as C six with six waters, but that is a happy coincidence. What makes it a carbohydrate is the aldehyde group and the hydroxyls, not the arithmetic of the formula.
<curious>Body इतने अलग अलग sugars एक साथ क्यों रखती है?</curious> एक busy Saturday market सोचो। हर carbohydrate समझने के लिए बस एक image चाहिए: market में पैसा कैसे चलता है।
Glucose है loose change. यह वो small-change currency है जो हर cell तुरंत energy के लिए spend कर सकती है, बिना किसी देरी।
दिन के अंत में vendor कमाई का wad बनाकर almirah में lock कर देता है। वो है starch plants में और glycogen animals में: energy एक storable form में folded, ज़रूरत पड़ने पर ही वापस coins बनती है।
लकड़ी का shelf और cotton kurta — वो cellulose है: sugar units जुड़ी हैं energy के लिए नहीं, बल्कि सिर्फ structure के लिए। Same bricks, बिलकुल अलग काम।
यह एक picture दिमाग़ में रखो: coins spend करने के लिए, locked wad store करने के लिए, shelf structure के लिए। Spend, store, structure — यही तीन पूरे chapter का सार पकड़ लेते हैं।

Chemically, carbohydrates हैं optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes या ketones, या ऐसे compounds जो hydrolysis पर यही units देते हैं। पुराना नाम इसी general formula से आया, क्योंकि ये carbon के hydrates जैसे दिखते थे।

पर इस formula को सिर्फ एक historical hint मानो, definition कभी नहीं। Acetic acid same pattern में fit होता है फिर भी sugar नहीं, और rhamnose असली sugar है जो fit नहीं होता। हमेशा functional-group definition पर भरोसा करो।
Glucose fit तो हो जाता है C six के साथ six waters के रूप में, पर यह बस एक coincidence है। इसे carbohydrate बनाता है aldehyde group और hydroxyls, वो formula का arithmetic नहीं।

board_events.text: A second, cross-cutting label: reducing vs non-reducing.
A free carbonyl reduces Tollens' or Fehling's reagent.
'Reducing' depends on a FREE carbonyl, not on mono- vs di-.

segments.text: Every carbohydrate is built from one repeating brick, a small sugar unit. The single question that fixes its class is: how many bricks can you knock loose by hydrolysis?
A monosaccharide is a single brick that cannot be hydrolysed into anything simpler. Glucose, fructose and ribose are the classic examples, and about twenty of them occur in nature.
An oligosaccharide carries two to ten bricks. The commonest are the disaccharides, sucrose, maltose and lactose, each hydrolysing into two monosaccharide units, either the same or different.
A polysaccharide strings together a large number of bricks. Starch, cellulose and glycogen are the examples. These are not sweet, which is why they are also called non-sugars.
So the primary classification is just a brick count: one, a handful, or many. Read this tree top to bottom and the whole family sorts itself out cleanly.
Cutting across that count is a second label. It asks whether a sugar still has a free reactive carbonyl end, a free aldehyde or keto group, that can act as a reducing agent.
If that free end exists, the sugar reduces Tollens' or Fehling's reagent and we call it a reducing sugar. If both reactive ends are locked into the joining bond, it is non-reducing.
Notice the trap already: reducing depends on a free carbonyl carbon, not merely on being a mono- or disaccharide. Maltose and lactose are reducing disaccharides, while sucrose is not.
हर carbohydrate एक repeating brick से बनी है, एक छोटी sugar unit। इसकी class तय करने वाला एक ही सवाल है: hydrolysis से कितनी bricks अलग हो सकती हैं?
Monosaccharide एक single brick है जो और छोटे में hydrolyse नहीं हो सकती। Glucose, fructose और ribose classic examples हैं, और nature में लगभग बीस पाए जाते हैं।
Oligosaccharide में दो से दस bricks होती हैं। सबसे common हैं disaccharides — sucrose, maltose और lactose — हर एक hydrolysis पर दो monosaccharide units देती है, same या different।
Polysaccharide बहुत सारी bricks जोड़ती है। Starch, cellulose और glycogen examples हैं। ये मीठे नहीं होते, इसीलिए इन्हें non-sugars भी कहते हैं।
तो primary classification बस एक brick count है: एक, कुछ, या बहुत सारी। इस tree को ऊपर से नीचे पढ़ो और पूरा family साफ़ sort हो जाता है।
इस count के across एक दूसरा label चलता है। यह पूछता है कि sugar के पास अब भी एक free reactive carbonyl end है या नहीं — एक free aldehyde या keto group — जो reducing agent की तरह काम कर सके।
अगर वो free end मौजूद है, तो sugar Tollens' या Fehling's reagent को reduce करती है और हम उसे reducing sugar कहते हैं। अगर दोनों reactive ends joining bond में locked हैं, तो वो non-reducing है।
Trap यहीं दिख जाता है: reducing depend करता है एक free carbonyl carbon पर, सिर्फ mono या disaccharide होने पर नहीं। Maltose और lactose reducing disaccharides हैं, जबकि sucrose नहीं।

board_events.text: It is the single most important bond in the whole topic.
The bridged carbons decide: reducing, branching, digestibility.
Non-reducing = both anomeric ends locked in the bond.
Reducing = at least one anomeric end still free.
Same condensation idea returns for proteins and nucleic acids.

segments.text: <curious>What exactly happens when two sugars join?</curious> The intuition is a handshake. A reducing sugar is a shopkeeper who keeps one counter open for business; a non-reducing sugar has both partners' hands clasped, so no counter is free.

When two monosaccharides join, one hydroxyl from each comes together, a water molecule is squeezed out, and an oxygen bridge, an oxide linkage, ties the two units. That bridge is the glycosidic linkage.
Here is that handshake drawn out: unit A and unit B, an oxygen bridge between them, and a water molecule lost in the process. Follow the bridge and you can already read the sugar's behaviour.
This is the single most important bond in the whole topic, because which carbons are bridged decides three things at once.
It decides whether the sugar still reduces, how a polysaccharide branches, and whether your body can even digest it. One bond, three consequences.
So a non-reducing sugar like sucrose is exactly the case where both partners' reactive anomeric ends are the ones tied up in the joining handshake, leaving no free counter for Tollens' or Fehling's.
A reducing sugar, by contrast, keeps at least one anomeric end free and open, which is why maltose and lactose still respond to the reagents while sucrose stays silent.
Keep this handshake-with-a-dropped-water-drop in mind. The very same condensation idea returns later as the peptide bond in proteins and the phosphodiester bond in nucleic acids.

<curious>जब दो sugars जुड़ते हैं तो असल में होता क्या है?</curious> Intuition एक handshake है। Reducing sugar वो shopkeeper है जो एक counter खुला रखता है; non-reducing sugar में दोनों partners के हाथ clasped हैं, तो कोई counter free नहीं।
जब दो monosaccharides जुड़ते हैं, हर एक से एक hydroxyl आता है, एक water molecule बाहर निकलती है, और एक oxygen bridge — oxide linkage — दोनों units को बाँध देता है। वही bridge glycosidic linkage है।
यह handshake यहाँ drawn है: unit A और unit B, बीच में oxygen bridge, और process में एक water molecule lost। Bridge को follow करो और sugar का behaviour पहले से पढ़ सकते हो।
यह पूरे topic का सबसे important bond है, क्योंकि कौन से carbons bridge हुए हैं यह एक साथ तीन चीज़ें तय करता है।
यह तय करता है कि sugar अब भी reduce करती है या नहीं, polysaccharide कैसे branch होती है, और आपका body इसे digest कर सकता है या नहीं। एक bond, तीन consequences।
तो sucrose जैसी non-reducing sugar exactly वो case है जहाँ दोनों partners के reactive anomeric ends ही joining handshake में बँधे हैं, Tollens' या Fehling's के लिए कोई free counter नहीं छोड़ते।
इसके उलट reducing sugar कम से कम एक anomeric end free और open रखती है, इसीलिए maltose और lactose reagents को respond करती हैं जबकि sucrose चुप रहती है।
इस handshake-with-a-dropped-water-drop को याद रखो। यही condensation idea बाद में proteins में peptide bond और nucleic acids में phosphodiester bond बनकर लौटता है।

board_events.text: Combine with carbon count: aldohexose, ketohexose, aldopentose.
On cyclising, a sugar closes into a ring — and rings get names too.
Glucose forms the pyranose ring; fructose forms the furanose ring.
Memory hook: glucose-Pyranose (six), fructose-Furanose (five).

segments.text: A monosaccharide gets its full name from two facts stacked together: what kind of carbonyl it carries, and how many carbons sit in the chain.
An aldose carries an aldehyde group at the end of the chain. A ketose carries a keto group sitting inside the chain. That single difference splits the whole family in two.
See it side by side: glucose with its aldehyde at the top end, fructose with its keto group tucked one carbon in. Carbonyl at the end means aldose; carbonyl inside means ketose.

Now combine with the carbon count. A six-carbon aldose is an aldohexose, that is glucose. A six-carbon ketose is a ketohexose, that is fructose. A five-carbon aldose is an aldopentose, that is ribose.
These sugars rarely stay as open chains. In solution they curl up and close into rings, and the ring size earns its own name.
A six-membered sugar ring is a pyranose, named by analogy with pyran. A five-membered ring is a furanose, named by analogy with furan. The ring name is purely about how many atoms close the loop.
Lock this pairing in now, because examiners love to swap it: glucose forms the six-membered pyranose ring, and fructose forms the five-membered furanose ring.
A clean memory hook carries it into the exam hall: glucose goes with Pyranose, the six, and fructose goes with Furanose, the five. Matching first letters, matching sizes.
Monosaccharide अपना full name दो facts से पाती है, एक साथ stacked: उसका carbonyl किस तरह का है, और chain में कितने carbons हैं।
Aldose chain के end पर एक aldehyde group रखती है। Ketose chain के अंदर एक keto group रखती है। यही एक difference पूरे family को दो हिस्सों में बाँट देता है।
इसे side by side देखो: glucose अपने aldehyde के साथ top end पर, fructose अपने keto group के साथ एक carbon अंदर। Carbonyl end पर मतलब aldose; carbonyl अंदर मतलब ketose।
अब carbon count के साथ combine करो। Six-carbon aldose एक aldohexose है, यानी glucose। Six-carbon ketose एक ketohexose है, यानी fructose। Five-carbon aldose एक aldopentose है, यानी ribose।
ये sugars कम ही open chains रहती हैं। Solution में ये curl होकर rings में बंद हो जाती हैं, और ring का size अपना अलग नाम पाता है।
Six-membered sugar ring एक pyranose है, pyran की analogy से। Five-membered ring एक furanose है, furan की analogy से। Ring का नाम बस इस बात का है कि loop कितने atoms से बंद होता है।
इस pairing को अभी lock कर लो, क्योंकि examiners इसे swap करना पसंद करते हैं: glucose six-membered pyranose ring बनाती है, और fructose five-membered furanose ring बनाती है।
एक clean memory hook exam hall तक ले जाता है: glucose जाता है Pyranose के साथ, यानी six, और fructose जाता है Furanose के साथ, यानी five। पहले letters match, sizes match।

board_events.text: Ring closure creates one brand-new chiral centre
The old carbonyl carbon becomes the anomeric carbon.
Two ring forms differ only in the OH direction at this carbon.

board_events.text: Alpha means OH down; beta means OH up.
This tiny difference will decide starch versus cellulose.
The anomeric carbon is also the free reducing end.
One carbon quietly ties the chapter's ideas together.

segments.text: When the ring snaps shut, something subtle happens at exactly one carbon, and that carbon carries the whole story of anomers.
The carbon that was the carbonyl carbon before ring closure becomes a new chiral centre on cyclisation. In glucose that is C one; in fructose it is C two. We call it the anomeric carbon.
Because it is now chiral, its hydroxyl can point two ways. The two ring forms that differ only in the hydroxyl orientation at this one carbon are called anomers.

Here are the two, drawn as Haworth rings. In the alpha anomer the C one hydroxyl points down; in the beta anomer it points up. Look closely: everything else about the two molecules is completely identical.
So the label is narrow and precise. Alpha means the anomeric hydroxyl points down, beta means it points up. That is the entire meaning of the alpha and beta prefixes.
Do not underestimate this tiny difference. This same alpha-versus-beta orientation is exactly what will separate digestible starch from indigestible cellulose a few sections from now.
And here is the bridge back to reducing sugars: the anomeric carbon is precisely the reactive end. Leave it free and the sugar reduces; lock it into a glycosidic bond and it cannot.
So one quiet carbon ties three ideas together: it makes the ring chiral, it names the anomers, and it controls reducing power. Keep your eye on the anomeric carbon throughout.
जब ring बंद होती है, exactly एक carbon पर कुछ subtle होता है, और वही carbon anomers की पूरी कहानी रखता है।
जो carbon ring बंद होने से पहले carbonyl carbon था, cyclisation पर एक new chiral centre बन जाता है। Glucose में वो C one है; fructose में C two। इसे हम anomeric carbon कहते हैं।
अब यह chiral है, तो इसका hydroxyl दो तरफ point कर सकता है। जो दो ring forms सिर्फ इस एक carbon पर hydroxyl की orientation में differ करती हैं, उन्हें anomers कहते हैं।
ये रहे दोनों, Haworth rings के रूप में। Alpha anomer में C one का hydroxyl नीचे point करता है; beta anomer में ऊपर। ध्यान से देखो: बाकी सब कुछ दोनों molecules में बिलकुल identical है।
तो label narrow और precise है। Alpha मतलब anomeric hydroxyl नीचे, beta मतलब ऊपर। यही alpha और beta prefixes का पूरा मतलब है।
इस tiny difference को कम मत आँको। यही alpha-versus-beta orientation कुछ sections आगे digestible starch को indigestible cellulose से अलग करेगा।
और यहाँ reducing sugars से जोड़ने वाला bridge है: anomeric carbon ही reactive end है। इसे free छोड़ो तो sugar reduce करती है; इसे glycosidic bond में lock करो तो नहीं कर सकती।
तो एक quiet carbon तीन ideas को जोड़ता है: यह ring को chiral बनाता है, anomers को नाम देता है, और reducing power control करता है। पूरे topic में anomeric carbon पर नज़र रखो।

segments.text: Most direct exam questions on this topic reduce to a single lookup: which units, joined at which carbons, and is a free end left. Let us build that rulebook for the named sugars.
Sucrose is alpha-D-glucose joined to beta-D-fructose, and the join is C one of glucose to C two of fructose. Both anomeric carbons are consumed in that bond, so sucrose is non-reducing.
Maltose is two alpha-D-glucose units joined C one to C four. Only one anomeric carbon is used, so the other stays free, and maltose is reducing.
Lactose is beta-D-galactose joined to beta-D-glucose, C one of galactose to C four of glucose. The glucose C one stays free, so lactose is reducing as well.

Contrast the two: in sucrose both reactive ends are tied into the C one to C two bond, so nothing is free. In maltose the C one to C four bond leaves one anomeric end open. That green dot is the whole difference.
Move to the polysaccharides. Starch is alpha-D-glucose in two flavours: amylose is a linear chain of C one to C four links, while amylopectin adds C one to C six branch points.
Glycogen, the animal storage form, is also alpha-D-glucose with C one to C four chains and C one to C six branches, but far more highly branched than amylopectin.

Cellulose is the odd one out: beta-D-glucose in a linear C one to C four chain. Starch is alpha, cellulose is beta, and that single alpha-versus-beta switch is exactly why we digest starch but cannot digest cellulose.
इस topic के ज़्यादातर direct exam questions एक lookup पर सिमट जाते हैं: कौन सी units, किन carbons पर जुड़ी, और free end बचा या नहीं। इन्हीं named sugars के लिए वो rulebook बनाते हैं।
Sucrose है alpha-D-glucose जुड़ा beta-D-fructose से, और join है glucose के C one से fructose के C two तक। दोनों anomeric carbons उस bond में खप जाते हैं, इसलिए sucrose non-reducing है।
Maltose है दो alpha-D-glucose units जुड़ी C one से C four तक। सिर्फ एक anomeric carbon use होता है, दूसरा free रहता है, इसलिए maltose reducing है।
Lactose है beta-D-galactose जुड़ा beta-D-glucose से, galactose के C one से glucose के C four तक। Glucose का C one free रहता है, इसलिए lactose भी reducing है।

दोनों को contrast करो: sucrose में दोनों reactive ends C one to C two bond में बँधे हैं, कुछ free नहीं। Maltose में C one to C four bond एक anomeric end खुला छोड़ता है। वो हरा dot ही पूरा difference है।
अब polysaccharides पर आओ। Starch है alpha-D-glucose दो रूपों में: amylose एक linear chain है C one to C four links की, जबकि amylopectin C one to C six branch points जोड़ती है।
Glycogen, animal storage form, भी alpha-D-glucose है — C one to C four chains और C one to C six branches के साथ, पर amylopectin से कहीं ज़्यादा highly branched।
Cellulose अलग है: beta-D-glucose एक linear C one to C four chain में। Starch alpha है, cellulose beta, और यही एक alpha-versus-beta switch वजह है कि हम starch digest करते हैं पर cellulose नहीं।

First, how glucose is made: from sucrose or from starch.
Heating with HI gives n-hexane: a straight six-carbon chain.
Oxime and cyanohydrin confirm a carbonyl; bromine water pins an aldehyde.
Acetylation gives a penta-acetate: five hydroxyls on five carbons.

segments.text: There is a beautiful chain of chemical reasoning here. Reproducing the logic, not just the final structure, is what separates a full-mark board answer from a half one.

First note the two standard routes. Boiling sucrose with dilute acid in alcohol gives equal amounts of glucose and fructose. Commercially, starch is hydrolysed with dilute sulphuric acid at about three hundred ninety three kelvin under two to three atmospheres.

Now the evidence. Prolonged heating with hydrogen iodide strips every oxygen function down to hydrocarbon and yields n-hexane. A straight six-carbon alkane proves all six carbons sit in one unbranched chain.

Reaction with hydroxylamine gives an oxime and with hydrogen cyanide a cyanohydrin, so a carbonyl is present. Mild oxidation with bromine water gives gluconic acid, and since bromine water oxidises only an aldehyde, that carbonyl is specifically a terminal aldehyde.

Acetylation with acetic anhydride installs five acetyl groups, giving a stable penta-acetate. Five acetyls means five hydroxyl groups, and because the product is stable, they sit on five different carbons.

Oxidation with concentrated nitric acid turns both glucose and gluconic acid into the same dicarboxylic acid, saccharic acid, so the far end must have been a primary alcohol. Assemble every clue and you reach the Fischer skeleton on the board.

Here is the assembled structure: aldehyde on top, primary alcohol at the bottom, four hydroxyls in between with fixed left-right placements. The lowest asymmetric carbon, C five, carries its hydroxyl on the right.

Finally, why D and why plus. The D label compares C five with glyceraldehyde: hydroxyl on the right means D. The plus sign is a separate experimental fact, that it rotates light clockwise. A D sugar can rotate either way, so never fuse the two.
यहाँ chemical reasoning की एक खूबसूरत chain है। सिर्फ final structure नहीं, बल्कि logic को reproduce करना ही full-mark board answer को half से अलग करता है।

पहले दो standard routes note करो। Sucrose को dilute acid के साथ alcohol में उबालो तो बराबर मात्रा में glucose और fructose मिलता है। Commercially, starch को dilute sulphuric acid के साथ लगभग three hundred ninety three kelvin पर two to three atmospheres में hydrolyse किया जाता है।

अब evidence। Hydrogen iodide के साथ prolonged heating हर oxygen function को hydrocarbon तक strip कर देता है और n-hexane देता है। एक straight six-carbon alkane साबित करता है कि सभी six carbons एक unbranched chain में हैं।

Hydroxylamine के साथ reaction एक oxime देता है और hydrogen cyanide के साथ cyanohydrin, तो एक carbonyl मौजूद है। Bromine water से mild oxidation gluconic acid देता है, और चूँकि bromine water सिर्फ aldehyde को oxidise करता है, वो carbonyl specifically एक terminal aldehyde है।
Acetic anhydride से acetylation पाँच acetyl groups लगाता है, एक stable penta-acetate देकर। पाँच acetyls मतलब पाँच hydroxyl groups, और चूँकि product stable है, ये पाँच अलग carbons पर हैं।

Concentrated nitric acid से oxidation glucose और gluconic acid दोनों को एक ही dicarboxylic acid, saccharic acid, में बदल देता है, तो दूर वाला end एक primary alcohol रहा होगा। हर clue जोड़ो और तुम board पर दिख रहे Fischer skeleton तक पहुँचते हो।
यह रहा assembled structure: ऊपर aldehyde, नीचे primary alcohol, बीच में चार hydroxyls fixed left-right placements के साथ। सबसे नीचे वाला asymmetric carbon, C five, अपना hydroxyl दाईं ओर रखता है।

आख़िर में, D क्यों और plus क्यों। D label C five की तुलना glyceraldehyde से करता है: hydroxyl दाईं ओर मतलब D। Plus sign एक अलग experimental fact है, कि यह light को clockwise घुमाता है। D sugar किसी भी तरफ घुमा सकती है, तो दोनों को कभी मत मिलाओ।

board_events.text: The aldehyde is 'mostly hidden', so open-chain reactions partly fail.
This slow re-equilibration is mutarotation.

segments.text: The open-chain picture is elegant, but three stubborn facts simply refuse to fit a free aldehyde. They force an upgrade.
First, glucose gives no Schiff's test and forms no hydrogensulphite addition product with sodium bisulphite, even though ordinary aldehydes readily do both.
Second, the penta-acetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine at all, as if the aldehyde had simply vanished.

Third, glucose crystallises in two distinct forms, an alpha form melting near four hundred nineteen kelvin and a beta form melting near four hundred twenty three kelvin. A single open chain cannot explain two crystals.
The resolution is elegant. The hydroxyl at C five swings round and adds across the aldehyde carbon, forming a cyclic hemiacetal and closing a six-membered pyranose ring.

Here is the full picture. In solution the open chain sits in equilibrium with the alpha and beta rings. The former aldehyde carbon, C one, becomes the anomeric carbon, and its two orientations give the alpha and beta anomers.
Because the equilibrium keeps the aldehyde mostly hidden inside rings, the open-chain reactions only partly succeed. That is exactly why the Schiff and bisulphite tests come up short.
And this same open-to-ring interconversion, the alpha and beta forms slowly settling to their equilibrium ratio, is what we later meet as mutarotation, a slow drift in optical rotation on standing.
Open-chain picture elegant है, पर तीन ज़िद्दी facts एक free aldehyde में fit ही नहीं होते। ये एक upgrade मजबूर कर देते हैं।
पहला, glucose न Schiff's test देता है और न sodium bisulphite के साथ hydrogensulphite addition product बनाता है, जबकि ordinary aldehydes दोनों आसानी से करते हैं।
दूसरा, glucose का penta-acetate hydroxylamine के साथ बिलकुल react नहीं करता, मानो aldehyde गायब ही हो गया हो।

तीसरा, glucose दो अलग crystalline forms में crystallise होता है — एक alpha form जो लगभग four hundred nineteen kelvin पर पिघलता है और एक beta form लगभग four hundred twenty three kelvin पर। एक single open chain दो crystals नहीं समझा सकता।
Resolution elegant है। C five का hydroxyl घूमकर aldehyde carbon के across add हो जाता है, एक cyclic hemiacetal बनाकर और एक six-membered pyranose ring बंद करके।

यह रहा पूरा picture। Solution में open chain alpha और beta rings के साथ equilibrium में रहता है। पुराना aldehyde carbon, C one, anomeric carbon बन जाता है, और इसकी दो orientations alpha और beta anomers देती हैं।
चूँकि equilibrium aldehyde को ज़्यादातर rings के अंदर छिपाए रखता है, open-chain reactions सिर्फ आंशिक रूप से चलती हैं। इसीलिए Schiff और bisulphite tests अधूरे रह जाते हैं।
और यही open-to-ring interconversion — alpha और beta forms धीरे धीरे अपने equilibrium ratio पर बैठना — वही है जिसे हम आगे mutarotation कहते हैं, standing पर optical rotation में एक slow drift।

board_events.text: Same formula, a keto group, a five-membered ring
Fructose is a ketohexose: keto group at C2.
Its C5 hydroxyl adds to the C2 keto carbon.

board_events.text: It belongs to the D-series but is laevorotatory: D-(minus)-fructose.
Glucose: aldo, pyranose, C1 anomeric. Fructose: keto, furanose, C2 anomeric.
Both are the monosaccharide bricks that build sucrose.

segments.text: Fructose runs the whole glucose story in parallel, with two neat swaps. Same molecular formula, but a keto group instead of an aldehyde.
Fructose shares the formula C six H twelve O six with glucose, but its carbonyl is a keto group at C two, which makes it a ketohexose rather than an aldohexose.
Just as glucose cyclised, the C five hydroxyl of fructose adds to the C two keto carbon. But because the keto group sits at C two, the ring that closes is smaller.
Here is the result: a five-membered furanose ring. The anomeric carbon is now C two, the old keto carbon, and just like glucose it comes in alpha and beta anomers.

Fructose belongs to the D-series yet rotates plane-polarised light to the left, so its full name is D-minus-fructose. This is the cleanest reminder that the D letter and the rotation sign are independent.

Hold the two side by side. Glucose is an aldohexose, a pyranose, anomeric carbon C one. Fructose is a ketohexose, a furanose, anomeric carbon C two. That contrast answers a great many quick questions.
And these two monosaccharides are not strangers: glucose and fructose are precisely the two bricks that clasp hands to build sucrose, which brings the whole thread of this part full circle.
Fructose पूरी glucose story parallel में चलाती है, दो neat swaps के साथ। Same molecular formula, पर aldehyde की जगह एक keto group।
Fructose glucose के साथ formula C six H twelve O six share करती है, पर इसका carbonyl C two पर एक keto group है, जो इसे aldohexose नहीं बल्कि ketohexose बनाता है।
जैसे glucose cyclise हुई, fructose का C five hydroxyl C two keto carbon पर add होता है। पर चूँकि keto group C two पर है, जो ring बंद होती है वो छोटी है।
यह रहा result: एक five-membered furanose ring। Anomeric carbon अब C two है, पुराना keto carbon, और glucose की तरह यह भी alpha और beta anomers में आती है।
Fructose D-series की है फिर भी plane-polarised light को बाईं ओर घुमाती है, तो इसका पूरा नाम D-minus-fructose है। यह सबसे साफ़ reminder है कि D letter और rotation sign independent हैं।

दोनों को साथ रखो। Glucose एक aldohexose है, एक pyranose, anomeric carbon C one। Fructose एक ketohexose है, एक furanose, anomeric carbon C two। यह contrast बहुत सारे quick questions का जवाब दे देता है।
और ये दोनों monosaccharides अजनबी नहीं हैं: glucose और fructose ही वो दो bricks हैं जो हाथ मिलाकर sucrose बनाती हैं, जिससे इस part का पूरा thread full circle हो जाता है।

board_events.text: The diagnostic numbers worth memorising
D/L is configuration; the (+)/(-) sign is measured rotation. They are independent.
This is a restated toolkit — a formula recap for the full chapter comes at the very end.

segments.text: Carbohydrates carry no dimensional formulae, so the numbers to memorise are the molecular identities, the specific rotations, and a few key reactions. Here is that compact toolkit.
First the identities. Glucose and fructose share C six H twelve O six. Sucrose is C twelve H twenty two O eleven. Starch and cellulose repeat the unit C six H ten O five, n times.

Next the specific rotations, which drive the invert-sugar logic. Glucose is plus fifty two point five degrees, fructose is minus ninety two point four degrees, and sucrose is plus sixty six point five degrees.

A crucial caution sits alongside these: the D and L letters describe configuration, while the plus and minus sign is the measured direction of rotation. D-glucose is plus, D-fructose is minus, decided by completely different criteria.
For preparation from sucrose: boil with dilute acid and it hydrolyses into equal amounts of glucose and fructose. This is the reaction behind invert sugar.
For the commercial route from starch: hydrolyse with dilute sulphuric acid at about three hundred ninety three kelvin under two to three atmospheres, and each repeat unit yields one glucose.

Finally the invert-sugar arithmetic. An equimolar glucose-fructose mixture has rotation near the average of the two, roughly minus twenty degrees, which is laevorotatory. The sign has flipped from the plus sixty six of sucrose.
Treat this as your complete carbohydrate toolkit, restated for quick reference, not re-taught. The consolidated formula recap for the entire chapter arrives right at the very end of the last part.
Carbohydrates के पास dimensional formulae नहीं हैं, तो याद रखने वाले numbers हैं molecular identities, specific rotations, और कुछ key reactions। यह रहा वो compact toolkit।
पहले identities। Glucose और fructose C six H twelve O six share करते हैं। Sucrose है C twelve H twenty two O eleven। Starch और cellulose unit C six H ten O five को n बार दोहराते हैं।
अब specific rotations, जो invert-sugar logic चलाते हैं। Glucose plus fifty two point five degrees, fructose minus ninety two point four degrees, और sucrose plus sixty six point five degrees।
इनके साथ एक ज़रूरी caution है: D और L letters configuration बताते हैं, जबकि plus और minus sign rotation की measured direction है। D-glucose plus है, D-fructose minus, बिलकुल अलग criteria से तय।
Sucrose से preparation के लिए: dilute acid के साथ उबालो और यह बराबर मात्रा में glucose और fructose में hydrolyse हो जाती है। यही reaction invert sugar के पीछे है।
Starch से commercial route के लिए: dilute sulphuric acid के साथ लगभग three hundred ninety three kelvin पर two to three atmospheres में hydrolyse करो, और हर repeat unit एक glucose देता है।

आख़िर में invert-sugar arithmetic। एक equimolar glucose-fructose mixture का rotation दोनों के average के पास होता है, लगभग minus twenty degrees, जो laevorotatory है। Sign sucrose के plus sixty six से flip हो चुका है।
इसे अपना complete carbohydrate toolkit समझो, quick reference के लिए restated, दोबारा पढ़ाया नहीं गया। पूरे chapter का consolidated formula recap आख़िरी part के बिलकुल अंत में आता है।

board_events.text: Bromine water is a mild oxidant that attacks only an aldehyde.
Product A = gluconic acid, so the carbonyl is a terminal aldehyde.

Product B = penta-acetate, so five hydroxyls sit on five carbons.
Prolonged HI reduces every oxygen function to hydrocarbon.
Answer: gluconic acid, penta-acetate, n-hexane — aldehyde, five OH, straight C6.

segments.text: Here is a clean board-level question. A pure sample of D-glucose is split into three portions and treated with bromine water, with excess acetic anhydride, and with prolonged heating with hydrogen iodide. Name each product and give the one structural fact it supports.
Picture the three branches at once. Each reagent attacks a different feature of the molecule, so each product reports a different piece of the structure.
Start with bromine water. It is a mild oxidant that attacks only an aldehyde, never a ketone, so it selectively targets glucose's carbonyl end.
The product is gluconic acid, a six-carbon monocarboxylic acid. Conclusion one: the carbonyl in glucose is a terminal aldehydic group.
Next, acetic anhydride acetylates hydroxyl groups. However many hydroxyls exist, that many acetyl groups go on.
The product is glucose penta-acetate, with five acetyl groups installed. Conclusion two: glucose contains five hydroxyl groups on five different carbons.
Finally, prolonged heating with hydrogen iodide reduces every oxygen function all the way down to hydrocarbon.

The product is n-hexane. Conclusion three: the six carbons form a straight unbranched chain. So the answer is gluconic acid, penta-acetate, and n-hexane, supporting a terminal aldehyde, five hydroxyls, and a straight six-carbon chain.

यह रहा एक clean board-level question। D-glucose का एक pure sample तीन हिस्सों में बाँटकर bromine water, excess acetic anhydride, और hydrogen iodide के साथ prolonged heating से treat किया जाता है। हर product का नाम दो और वो एक structural fact बताओ जो यह support करता है।
तीनों branches एक साथ picture करो। हर reagent molecule के अलग feature पर हमला करता है, तो हर product structure का अलग टुकड़ा बताता है।
Bromine water से शुरू करो। यह एक mild oxidant है जो सिर्फ aldehyde पर हमला करता है, ketone पर कभी नहीं, तो यह selectively glucose के carbonyl end को target करता है।
Product है gluconic acid, एक six-carbon monocarboxylic acid। Conclusion एक: glucose का carbonyl एक terminal aldehydic group है।
अब acetic anhydride hydroxyl groups को acetylate करता है। जितने hydroxyls हैं, उतने acetyl groups लगते हैं।
Product है glucose penta-acetate, पाँच acetyl groups के साथ। Conclusion दो: glucose में पाँच hydroxyl groups हैं, पाँच अलग carbons पर।
आख़िर में hydrogen iodide के साथ prolonged heating हर oxygen function को पूरी तरह hydrocarbon तक reduce कर देता है।

Product है n-hexane। Conclusion तीन: छह carbons एक straight unbranched chain बनाते हैं। तो answer है gluconic acid, penta-acetate, और n-hexane, जो support करते हैं एक terminal aldehyde, पाँच hydroxyls, और एक straight six-carbon chain।

board_events.text: Maltose: glucose-glucose C1 to C4, one anomeric carbon free — reducing.
Lactose: galactose-glucose C1 to C4, glucose C1 free — reducing.
Fructose: a free monosaccharide with a free keto group — reducing.
Sucrose: joined C1-glucose to C2-fructose, both ends locked — non-reducing.
Answer: three (maltose, lactose, fructose). Sucrose is the famous exception.

segments.text: Here is a fast N E E T-style trap. Among maltose, sucrose, lactose and D-fructose, how many are reducing sugars? The options are one, two, three or four.
The trap is reflexive. Students tag every disaccharide as non-reducing and every monosaccharide as reducing, then mis-count. Do not sort by class; sort by whether a free carbonyl end survives.
Run the free-end check across all four at once. Three of them keep an anomeric end open; only one has both ends locked.
Maltose is glucose joined to glucose C one to C four, so one anomeric carbon stays free. Reducing.
Lactose is galactose joined to glucose C one to C four, and the glucose C one stays free. Reducing.
Fructose is a free monosaccharide with a free keto group, so it is reducing too.
Sucrose is joined C one of glucose to C two of fructose, locking both reducing ends. Non-reducing, and the lone exception here.
Count the reducing ones: maltose, lactose and fructose make three. The answer is three. The mental shortcut is that of the common sugars, sucrose is the one famous non-reducing exception.
यह रहा एक तेज़ N E E T-style trap। Maltose, sucrose, lactose और D-fructose में से कितनी reducing sugars हैं? Options हैं one, two, three या four।
Trap reflexive है। Students हर disaccharide को non-reducing और हर monosaccharide को reducing tag कर देते हैं, फिर गलत गिनते हैं। Class से मत sort करो; इससे करो कि free carbonyl end बचा या नहीं।
चारों पर एक साथ free-end check चलाओ। तीन एक anomeric end खुला रखती हैं; सिर्फ एक के दोनों ends locked हैं।
Maltose है glucose जुड़ा glucose से C one to C four, तो एक anomeric carbon free रहता है। Reducing।
Lactose है galactose जुड़ा glucose से C one to C four, और glucose का C one free रहता है। Reducing।
Fructose एक free monosaccharide है free keto group के साथ, तो यह भी reducing है।
Sucrose जुड़ा है glucose के C one से fructose के C two तक, दोनों reducing ends lock करके। Non-reducing, और यहाँ अकेला exception।
Reducing वाली गिनो: maltose, lactose और fructose मिलकर तीन। Answer है three। Mental shortcut यह है कि common sugars में sucrose ही एक famous non-reducing exception है।

board_events.text: For an equimolar mix, net rotation tracks the simple average.

That dextro-to-laevo inversion is why it is called invert sugar.
One C1-C2 bond ties structure (non-reducing) and optics (sign flip) together.

segments.text: Now a J E E Main level question linking optical arithmetic with structure. A chemist hydrolyses sucrose, which reads plus sixty six point five degrees, into an equimolar mix of glucose at plus fifty two point five and fructose at minus ninety two point four. Predict the mixture's sign and explain the name invert sugar.
Picture it on a number line. Sucrose starts firmly on the positive side. After hydrolysis the mixture lands well on the negative side. The instrument literally watches the sign flip.
For part one, an equimolar product mixture has a net observed rotation that tracks the simple average of the two component specific rotations.
Averaging plus fifty two point five with minus ninety two point four gives roughly minus twenty degrees. The result is negative, so the mixture is laevorotatory.

For part two, the starting sucrose was dextrorotatory at plus sixty six point five, while the product mixture is laevorotatory near minus twenty. Hydrolysis has inverted the sign of optical rotation from plus to minus.
That dextro-to-laevo reversal on hydrolysis is exactly why the product is historically named invert sugar.

And the deeper link: the very same C one to C two glycosidic bond that makes sucrose non-reducing is the bond hydrolysis breaks. Breaking it frees fructose, whose large negative rotation overwhelms glucose's modest positive one. Structure and optics are two faces of one bond.

अब एक J E E Main level question जो optical arithmetic को structure से जोड़ता है। एक chemist sucrose को, जो plus sixty six point five degrees पढ़ता है, glucose plus fifty two point five और fructose minus ninety two point four के equimolar mix में hydrolyse करता है। Mixture का sign predict करो और invert sugar नाम समझाओ।
इसे एक number line पर picture करो। Sucrose मज़बूती से positive side पर शुरू होती है। Hydrolysis के बाद mixture negative side पर आ जाता है। Instrument सचमुच sign को flip होते देखता है।
Part one के लिए, एक equimolar product mixture का net observed rotation दोनों component specific rotations के simple average को track करता है।
Plus fifty two point five को minus ninety two point four के साथ average करने पर लगभग minus twenty degrees आता है। Result negative है, तो mixture laevorotatory है।

Part two के लिए, शुरुआती sucrose dextrorotatory था plus sixty six point five पर, जबकि product mixture laevorotatory है लगभग minus twenty पर। Hydrolysis ने optical rotation का sign plus से minus में invert कर दिया।
Hydrolysis पर वही dextro-to-laevo reversal ही वजह है कि product को historically invert sugar कहते हैं।

और गहरा link: वही C one to C two glycosidic bond जो sucrose को non-reducing बनाता है, वही bond hydrolysis तोड़ता है। इसे तोड़ने से fructose free होती है, जिसका बड़ा negative rotation glucose के modest positive को दबा देता है। Structure और optics एक ही bond के दो चेहरे हैं।

board_events.text: An internal mirror makes the molecule meso — optically inactive.
So X's four internal centres must be end-to-end symmetric.
Glucose's aldaric acid (saccharic acid) is optically active — not meso.
X cannot be glucose; a galactose-type configuration fits (mucic acid is meso).

segments.text: Here is a J E E Advanced puzzle. An unknown D-aldohexose X, with the usual straight-chain skeleton, is oxidised at both ends by concentrated nitric acid to an aldaric acid Y. Y turns out to be optically inactive, a meso compound, whereas glucose's aldaric acid is optically active. Deduce a constraint on X, and say whether X can be glucose.
Step one, what the oxidation does. Concentrated nitric acid oxidises both the aldehyde end and the primary alcohol end to carboxyl groups, so Y has identical end groups, a diacid.

Here is the key geometry. Both ends are now the same carboxyl group, and if the four internal stereocentres are arranged so the top half mirrors the bottom half, an internal plane of symmetry appears.
When that internal mirror exists, the molecule is meso: it is superimposable on its own mirror image, and therefore optically inactive, even though it still contains chiral centres.

Apply this to X. Because Y is meso, the four stereocentres of X must be configured so that, once both ends become carboxyls, the top half mirrors the bottom. In Fischer terms the internal pattern must read the same forwards and backwards.
Step four, can X be glucose? The aldaric acid of D-glucose, saccharic acid, is optically active, meaning it lacks that mirror symmetry.

Since X's aldaric acid is meso and glucose's is not, X cannot be glucose. X must be an aldohexose whose end-to-end oxidation gives a symmetric meso diacid, and galactose is the classic example, since its aldaric acid, mucic acid, is optically inactive.

यह रहा एक J E E Advanced puzzle। एक unknown D-aldohexose X, सामान्य straight-chain skeleton के साथ, concentrated nitric acid से दोनों ends पर oxidise होकर एक aldaric acid Y बनाती है। Y निकलती है optically inactive, एक meso compound, जबकि glucose का aldaric acid optically active है। X पर एक constraint निकालो, और बताओ X glucose हो सकती है या नहीं।
Step एक, oxidation करता क्या है। Concentrated nitric acid aldehyde end और primary alcohol end दोनों को carboxyl groups में oxidise करता है, तो Y के end groups identical हैं, एक diacid।
यह रही key geometry। दोनों ends अब एक ही carboxyl group हैं, और अगर चार internal stereocentres इस तरह arranged हों कि top half bottom half को mirror करे, तो एक internal plane of symmetry दिख जाता है।
जब वो internal mirror मौजूद हो, molecule meso है: यह अपने ही mirror image पर superimposable है, इसलिए optically inactive, भले ही इसमें chiral centres हों।

इसे X पर लागू करो। चूँकि Y meso है, X के चार stereocentres इस तरह configured होने चाहिए कि दोनों ends carboxyl बनने पर top half bottom को mirror करे। Fischer terms में internal pattern आगे और पीछे एक जैसा पढ़ना चाहिए।
Step चार, क्या X glucose हो सकती है? D-glucose का aldaric acid, saccharic acid, optically active है, यानी उसमें वो mirror symmetry नहीं है।

चूँकि X का aldaric acid meso है और glucose का नहीं, X glucose नहीं हो सकती। X वो aldohexose होगी जिसकी end-to-end oxidation एक symmetric meso diacid देती है, और galactose classic example है, क्योंकि उसका aldaric acid, mucic acid, optically inactive है।

board_events.text: Sanity check: a twelve-carbon disaccharide yields two hexoses, never three.
Mnemonics: 'sucrose is the lone non-reducing sugar'; 'sweet-right to sour-left = invert'.

segments.text: <whisper>Here is where marks quietly leak away.</whisper> Four traps catch students on this topic again and again. Name each one and you defuse it.
Trap one: assuming all disaccharides are non-reducing. Only sucrose locks both reducing ends. Maltose and lactose each keep one free and are reducing. Anchor on the linkage, never the class.

Trap two: equating D and L with the plus and minus sign. The letter is relative configuration, judged against glyceraldehyde at the lowest asymmetric carbon. The sign is measured rotation. D-fructose is minus, D-glucose is plus.

Trap three: swapping pyranose with furanose, or alpha with beta. Glucose gives the six-membered pyranose, fructose the five-membered furanose. The alpha and beta labels refer only to the hydroxyl orientation at the anomeric carbon, nothing else.

Trap four: confusing cellulose with starch. Both are glucose polymers, but cellulose is beta-D-glucose, linear C one to C four, indigestible to us, while starch is alpha-D-glucose. That alpha-versus-beta switch is the digestibility switch.
For speed, burn in this two-step check for any hydrolysis or reducing question: first, which monosaccharides come out; second, is any anomeric carbon left free. Then add a carbon-count sanity test.
That carbon count catches careless answers instantly. A twelve-carbon disaccharide can only yield two hexose units, never three, because three hexoses would need eighteen carbons.

<whisper>Two mnemonics to carry in.</whisper> Sucrose is the lone famous non-reducing sugar, and sucrose goes from sweet-right to sour-left on hydrolysis, dextro to laevo, which is invert sugar. Those two lines answer a surprising share of the paper.
<whisper>यहीं marks चुपचाप बह जाते हैं।</whisper> चार traps इस topic पर students को बार बार पकड़ते हैं। हर एक को पहचानो और वो defuse हो जाता है।

Trap एक: यह मानना कि सभी disaccharides non-reducing हैं। सिर्फ sucrose दोनों reducing ends lock करती है। Maltose और lactose एक एक free रखती हैं और reducing हैं। Linkage पर anchor करो, class पर कभी नहीं।

Trap दो: D और L को plus और minus sign के बराबर मानना। Letter relative configuration है, glyceraldehyde से lowest asymmetric carbon पर judge किया गया। Sign measured rotation है। D-fructose minus है, D-glucose plus।

Trap तीन: pyranose को furanose से, या alpha को beta से swap करना। Glucose six-membered pyranose देती है, fructose five-membered furanose। Alpha और beta labels सिर्फ anomeric carbon पर hydroxyl orientation बताते हैं, और कुछ नहीं।

Trap चार: cellulose को starch से confuse करना। दोनों glucose polymers हैं, पर cellulose beta-D-glucose है, linear C one to C four, हमारे लिए indigestible, जबकि starch alpha-D-glucose है। वही alpha-versus-beta switch digestibility switch है।

Speed के लिए, किसी भी hydrolysis या reducing question के लिए यह two-step check याद कर लो: पहला, कौन सी monosaccharides निकलती हैं; दूसरा, कोई anomeric carbon free बचा या नहीं। फिर एक carbon-count sanity test जोड़ो।
वो carbon count careless answers तुरंत पकड़ लेता है। एक twelve-carbon disaccharide सिर्फ दो hexose units दे सकती है, तीन कभी नहीं, क्योंकि तीन hexoses को eighteen carbons चाहिए।

<whisper>दो mnemonics साथ ले जाओ।</whisper> Sucrose अकेली famous non-reducing sugar है, और sucrose hydrolysis पर sweet-right से sour-left जाती है, dextro से laevo, यानी invert sugar। ये दो lines paper का एक अच्छा हिस्सा answer कर देती हैं।

board_events.text: Sequence determines identity: the spine of the topic
Each letter is an amino acid: an acid and a base together
On the alpha-carbon, it becomes an alpha-amino acid
Only alpha-amino acids build proteins; about twenty are standard
Join enough letters and you spell a protein

segments.text: <curious>Why does changing one tiny unit in a protein change everything?</curious> Think of the twenty standard amino acids as the letters of an alphabet. The same letters in a different order spell a different word.
Take the letters T, E and A. In one order they read tea; rearranged they read ate; rearranged again, eat. Same three letters, three completely different words.
The cell does exactly this with amino acids. Rearrange the sequence and you do not get a slightly different protein; you get a different protein with a different job entirely.
That single idea, sequence determines identity, is the spine of this whole subtopic. Hold on to it, because every structural level we meet traces straight back to it.
Now the letter itself. An amino acid is a small molecule carrying two opposite-natured groups on one skeleton: an acidic carboxyl group and a basic amino group.
When the amino group sits on the carbon right next to the carboxyl carbon, the alpha-carbon, we call it an alpha-amino acid. These are the only kind you get on hydrolysing a protein.
Lock that in: only alpha-amino acids build proteins, even though beta, gamma and delta amino acids also exist. About twenty of them make up the standard building set.
String more than one hundred of these letters together, above a molecular mass of about ten thousand units, and you have spelled out a protein. Next we watch how two letters actually join.
<curious>Protein में एक छोटी unit बदलने से सब कुछ क्यों बदल जाता है?</curious> बीस standard amino acids को एक alphabet के letters समझो। वही letters अलग order में एक अलग शब्द बनाते हैं।
जैसे कमल और मलक — वही aksharas, अलग क्रम, अलग शब्द। Same letters, अलग order, बिलकुल अलग meaning।
Cell amino acids के साथ बिलकुल यही करती है। Sequence rearrange करो तो थोड़ा अलग protein नहीं मिलता; एक बिलकुल अलग protein मिलता है, अलग काम के साथ।
यही एक idea, sequence determines identity, पूरे subtopic की रीढ़ है। इसे पकड़े रहो, क्योंकि हर structural level सीधे इसी पर लौटता है।
अब letter खुद। एक amino acid छोटी molecule है जो एक ही skeleton पर दो opposite-natured groups रखती है: एक acidic carboxyl group और एक basic amino group।
जब amino group carboxyl carbon के ठीक बगल वाले carbon पर बैठता है, alpha-carbon पर, हम इसे alpha-amino acid कहते हैं। Protein hydrolyse करने पर सिर्फ यही मिलते हैं।
इसे lock करो: सिर्फ alpha-amino acids proteins बनाते हैं, भले ही beta, gamma और delta amino acids भी मौजूद हों। इनमें से लगभग बीस standard building set बनाते हैं।
इनमें से एक सौ से ज़्यादा letters जोड़ो, लगभग दस हज़ार units के molecular mass से ऊपर, और तुमने एक protein spell कर दिया। आगे देखते हैं दो letters असल में कैसे जुड़ते हैं।

board_events.text: Amino on one side, carboxyl on the other, both on one carbon
Only R changes from one amino acid to the next
In glycine, R is simply a hydrogen
Glycine is the lone optically inactive amino acid
Every other standard amino acid is chiral
Natural amino acids are L; D/L is configuration, not sign

segments.text: Zoom right in on one letter. At its heart sits a single carbon, the alpha-carbon, and four things hang off it.
Here is the brick drawn out: the amino group on one side, the carboxyl group on the other, a hydrogen above, and the side chain R below. That is every amino acid's shared shape.
The amino group is basic, the carboxyl group is acidic, and both sit on the very same carbon. Keep that pairing in mind; it drives the very next section entirely.
The one thing that changes from one amino acid to the next is R, the side chain. Everything else is identical, so R alone decides an amino acid's personality.
Take the simplest case, glycine. Its side chain R is just a hydrogen atom, so its alpha-carbon ends up carrying two identical hydrogens.
That makes glycine the lone optically inactive exception. With two identical hydrogens the alpha-carbon is not asymmetric, so glycine is achiral. Examiners test this every single time.
Every other standard amino acid has four different groups on the alpha-carbon, so it is chiral and optically active. Glycine is the single break in that pattern.
One more caution to plant now: naturally occurring amino acids are the L form. But D and L describe configuration only, and say nothing about whether the molecule rotates light plus or minus.
एक letter पर zoom करो। इसके केंद्र में एक single carbon है, alpha-carbon, और इस पर चार चीज़ें लटकती हैं।
यह रही brick drawn out: एक तरफ amino group, दूसरी तरफ carboxyl group, ऊपर एक hydrogen, और नीचे side chain R। यही हर amino acid का shared shape है।
Amino group basic है, carboxyl group acidic, और दोनों बिलकुल एक ही carbon पर हैं। इस pairing को याद रखो; यही ठीक अगला section पूरा चलाता है।
एक amino acid से दूसरे में जो एक चीज़ बदलती है वो है R, side chain। बाकी सब identical है, तो R अकेला amino acid की personality तय करता है।
सबसे simple case लो, glycine। इसका side chain R बस एक hydrogen atom है, तो इसका alpha-carbon आख़िर में दो identical hydrogens रखता है।
यही glycine को अकेला optically inactive exception बनाता है। दो identical hydrogens के साथ alpha-carbon asymmetric नहीं है, तो glycine achiral है। Examiners इसे हर बार test करते हैं।
बाकी हर standard amino acid के alpha-carbon पर चार अलग groups होते हैं, तो वो chiral और optically active है। Glycine उस pattern में अकेला break है।
अभी एक और caution बो दो: naturally occurring amino acids L form हैं। पर D और L सिर्फ configuration बताते हैं, और यह नहीं कि molecule light को plus घुमाता है या minus।

board_events.text: An acid and a base sharing one body
Like a mandi trader who buys and sells at once
In water, COOH hands its proton to NH2

board_events.text: A dipolar ion: charged, yet neutral overall
This is why amino acids are salt-like solids
Amphoteric: it neutralises both added acid and base
Isoelectric point: the pH of zero net charge, no migration

segments.text: Because an amino acid carries both an acid and a base in one body, it behaves in a way neither an amine nor an acid alone ever would.
Picture a trader in a mandi who is at once a buyer and a seller. The two roles settle a deal inside the same person, and an amino acid does exactly that internally.
In water the carboxyl group hands its proton across to the amino group on the very same molecule. The proton simply moves from oxygen to nitrogen.
Here is that internal transfer. The neutral form on the left becomes the dipolar zwitter ion on the right, carrying a positive charge on nitrogen and a negative on oxygen at once.
The result is a zwitter ion. It carries a full positive and a full negative charge, yet it is electrically neutral overall, because the two charges exactly cancel.
This internal salt is why amino acids are crystalline, high-melting, water-soluble solids that behave like salts, rather than like the volatile amines or acids you might otherwise expect.
It is also amphoteric. Add acid and the negative carboxylate accepts a proton; add base and the positive ammonium donates one. It fights back against both.

Push that logic to one special pH and you reach the isoelectric point: the pH at which the molecule sits as the neutral zwitter ion, carries no net charge, and does not migrate to either electrode in a field.
चूँकि amino acid एक ही body में acid और base दोनों रखता है, यह ऐसे behave करता है जैसे न अकेला amine करता और न अकेला acid।
एक mandi के trader को सोचो जो एक साथ buyer और seller है। दोनों roles एक ही इंसान के अंदर deal settle कर लेते हैं, और amino acid बिलकुल यही अंदर से करता है।
पानी में carboxyl group अपना proton उसी molecule के amino group को पकड़ा देता है। Proton बस oxygen से nitrogen पर चला जाता है।
यह रहा वो internal transfer। बाईं ओर का neutral form दाईं ओर dipolar zwitter ion बन जाता है, nitrogen पर positive और oxygen पर negative charge एक साथ लेकर।
Result एक zwitter ion है। यह एक पूरा positive और एक पूरा negative charge रखता है, फिर भी overall electrically neutral है, क्योंकि दोनों charges बिलकुल cancel हो जाते हैं।
यही internal salt वजह है कि amino acids crystalline, high-melting, water-soluble solids हैं जो salts जैसे behave करते हैं, न कि उन volatile amines या acids जैसे जिनकी तुम वरना उम्मीद करो।
यह amphoteric भी है। Acid डालो तो negative carboxylate एक proton accept करता है; base डालो तो positive ammonium एक donate करता है। यह दोनों के ख़िलाफ़ लड़ता है।

इस logic को एक special pH तक ले जाओ और तुम isoelectric point तक पहुँचते हो: वो pH जहाँ molecule neutral zwitter ion के रूप में बैठता है, कोई net charge नहीं रखता, और field में किसी electrode की ओर migrate नहीं करता।

board_events.text: Axis one: how far the amino group sits from the carboxyl

Axis two: the acid-base nature of the side chain
Extra COOH acidic; extra NH2 basic; neither neutral
Axis three: essential versus non-essential
Non-essential ones the body makes for itself

segments.text: Amino acids can be classified along three completely independent axes. Keeping them separate stops most classification mistakes before they even start.
Here are all three side by side: where the amino group sits, what the side chain R is like, and whether the body can make the amino acid or must eat it.
The first axis is the position of the amino group, labelled alpha, beta, gamma or delta according to its distance from the carboxyl carbon.
But only one of those positions matters for us: only alpha-amino acids build proteins. The others exist, but they never appear in a protein chain.
The second axis reads the acid-base nature of R. You simply count the acidic and basic groups hidden inside the side chain.
An extra carboxyl in R makes it acidic, as in glutamic and aspartic acid. An extra amino makes it basic, as in lysine and arginine. Neither, and it is neutral, like glycine and alanine.
The third axis is dietary need. Essential amino acids cannot be synthesised by the body and must come from diet, such as valine, leucine and lysine.
Non-essential amino acids, by contrast, the body can make for itself. Notice the three axes never interfere: an amino acid's position, its R, and its dietary status are all decided separately.
Amino acids को तीन बिलकुल independent axes पर classify किया जा सकता है। इन्हें अलग रखना ज़्यादातर classification गलतियाँ शुरू होने से पहले ही रोक देता है।
यहाँ तीनों side by side हैं: amino group कहाँ बैठता है, side chain R कैसा है, और body amino acid बना सकती है या उसे खाना पड़ता है।
पहला axis amino group की position है, carboxyl carbon से दूरी के हिसाब से alpha, beta, gamma या delta label किया गया।
पर इनमें से सिर्फ एक position हमारे लिए मायने रखती है: सिर्फ alpha-amino acids proteins बनाते हैं। बाकी मौजूद हैं, पर protein chain में कभी नहीं आते।
दूसरा axis R की acid-base nature पढ़ता है। तुम बस side chain के अंदर छिपे acidic और basic groups गिनते हो।
R में एक extra carboxyl इसे acidic बनाता है, जैसे glutamic और aspartic acid में। एक extra amino इसे basic बनाता है, जैसे lysine और arginine में। कुछ नहीं, तो यह neutral है, जैसे glycine और alanine।
तीसरा axis dietary need है। Essential amino acids body नहीं बना सकती और इन्हें diet से आना पड़ता है, जैसे valine, leucine और lysine।
इसके उलट non-essential amino acids body खुद बना सकती है। ध्यान दो कि तीनों axes कभी interfere नहीं करते: amino acid की position, उसका R, और उसका dietary status सब अलग अलग तय होते हैं।

board_events.text: The amide bridge is the peptide linkage
Naming runs N-terminal on the left to C-terminal on the right
Length labels: oligopeptide, polypeptide, protein
Insulin has fifty one residues yet counts as a protein

segments.text: Now join the bricks. Exactly as two sugars clasped hands through a glycosidic linkage, two amino acids clasp hands through a peptide bond.
It is the very same condensation idea from carbohydrates. The carboxyl of one and the amino of the next combine, and a water molecule is squeezed out.
Here glycine and alanine come together. A water molecule leaves, and an amide bridge ties the two into a dipeptide called glycylalanine.
That amide bridge is the peptide linkage. Two units make a dipeptide, three a tripeptide, and a long chain builds all the way up to a protein.
The counting rule is clean and heavily tested. For a chain of n amino acids there are exactly n minus one peptide bonds, and exactly n minus one water molecules released on assembly.
Naming always runs from the N-terminal, the free amino end on the left, to the C-terminal, the free carboxyl end on the right. So glycylalanine means glycine's carboxyl joined to alanine's amino.
Length earns a label too. Two to nine residues is an oligopeptide, about ten to one hundred is a polypeptide, and more than one hundred residues, above roughly ten thousand mass units, is a protein.

One neat exception to memorise: insulin has only fifty one residues, yet it counts as a protein because it holds a definite, functional conformation. Definite shape, not just raw length, earns the name.
अब bricks जोड़ो। जैसे दो sugars glycosidic linkage से हाथ मिलाते थे, वैसे ही दो amino acids peptide bond से हाथ मिलाते हैं।
यह carbohydrates वाला बिलकुल वही condensation idea है। एक का carboxyl और अगले का amino मिलते हैं, और एक water molecule बाहर निकलती है।
यहाँ glycine और alanine साथ आते हैं। एक water molecule निकलती है, और एक amide bridge दोनों को एक dipeptide में बाँध देता है जिसे glycylalanine कहते हैं।
वो amide bridge ही peptide linkage है। दो units एक dipeptide बनाती हैं, तीन एक tripeptide, और एक लंबी chain पूरे protein तक बना देती है।
Counting rule साफ़ है और खूब test होता है। n amino acids की chain के लिए exactly n minus one peptide bonds होते हैं, और assembly पर exactly n minus one water molecules निकलते हैं।
Naming हमेशा N-terminal से चलता है, बाईं ओर free amino end, C-terminal तक, दाईं ओर free carboxyl end। तो glycylalanine का मतलब glycine का carboxyl जुड़ा alanine के amino से।
Length भी एक label पाती है। दो से नौ residues एक oligopeptide है, लगभग दस से एक सौ एक polypeptide, और एक सौ से ज़्यादा residues, लगभग दस हज़ार mass units से ऊपर, एक protein।

एक neat exception याद रखो: insulin में सिर्फ fifty one residues हैं, फिर भी यह protein गिना जाता है क्योंकि इसकी एक definite, functional conformation है। Definite shape, सिर्फ length नहीं, नाम दिलाती है।

board_events.text: Why the peptide bond refuses to twist

board_events.text: A partial double bond cannot rotate freely
Six atoms are held in one plane, trans favoured
Free rotation survives only at the alpha-carbons
Planarity is precisely what makes helices and sheets possible
Sequence channels shape, so order is decisive

segments.text: Here is a structural fact with huge consequences. The peptide bond is not a plain single bond, and that is exactly why proteins can fold into regular shapes.
The link between the carbonyl carbon and the nitrogen has about forty percent double-bond character. It sits somewhere between a single and a double bond.
See why on the board. The nitrogen's lone pair delocalises onto the carbonyl, and that shared electron cloud stiffens the link into a partial double bond.
And a double bond, even a partial one, cannot rotate freely. So the whole amide unit is frozen, unable to spin about that carbon-nitrogen axis.
The upshot is that the six atoms of the amide unit are locked coplanar, all lying in a single flat plane, with the trans arrangement clearly favoured.
Rotation does not vanish entirely; it survives only at the alpha-carbons, at the angles chemists call phi and psi. The rigid amide planes are strung together by these flexible hinges.
This planarity is not a curiosity; it is precisely what makes regular folding geometrically possible. Without flat, predictable amide units, neat helices and sheets could never form.

And because each plane is rigid, the only freedom left is at the alpha-carbons, and which turns are favourable depends on the side chains. So the sequence itself channels the shape, which is why order is biologically decisive.
यह रहा एक structural fact जिसके huge consequences हैं। Peptide bond एक plain single bond नहीं है, और यही वजह है कि proteins regular shapes में fold कर पाते हैं।
Carbonyl carbon और nitrogen के बीच का link लगभग forty percent double-bond character रखता है। यह single और double bond के बीच कहीं बैठता है।
Board पर देखो क्यों। Nitrogen का lone pair carbonyl पर delocalise होता है, और वो shared electron cloud link को एक partial double bond में सख़्त कर देता है।
और एक double bond, आंशिक भी, freely rotate नहीं कर सकती। तो पूरी amide unit frozen है, उस carbon-nitrogen axis पर घूम नहीं सकती।
नतीजा यह कि amide unit के छह atoms coplanar locked हैं, सब एक single flat plane में, और trans arrangement साफ़ favoured है।
Rotation पूरी तरह ख़त्म नहीं होती; यह सिर्फ alpha-carbons पर बचती है, उन angles पर जिन्हें chemists phi और psi कहते हैं। Rigid amide planes इन flexible hinges से जुड़े रहते हैं।
यह planarity कोई curiosity नहीं; यही regular folding को geometrically possible बनाती है। Flat, predictable amide units के बिना, neat helices और sheets कभी न बनें।

और चूँकि हर plane rigid है, बची हुई freedom सिर्फ alpha-carbons पर है, और कौन से turns favourable हैं यह side chains पर depend करता है। तो sequence खुद shape को channel करता है, इसीलिए order biologically decisive है।

board_events.text: Primary: the amino-acid sequence, held by peptide bonds
Secondary: alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet
In the helix, each C=O bonds to an N-H one turn along
Tertiary: the whole 3-D fold, fibrous or globular
Quaternary: several folded chains as one unit
Primary is covalent and tough; levels two to four lean on weak bonds

segments.text: A protein is not a floppy string; it folds through four layered levels of structure, each one building on the last.
Here are all four in sequence: the bare chain, then local coils and sheets, then the full three-dimensional fold, then several folded chains assembled together.
Primary structure is simply the sequence of amino acids, held together by covalent peptide bonds. Change one residue and the protein's identity changes.
Secondary structure is the first folding response. The planar peptide units hydrogen-bond into regular patterns: the coiled alpha-helix and the folded beta-pleated sheet.
In the alpha-helix the chain twists into a right-handed screw, and each backbone carbonyl hydrogen-bonds to an amine hydrogen one turn further along. In the sheet, extended chains bond side by side.
Tertiary structure packs that secondary shape into a compact three-dimensional form, either a fibrous rod or a globular ball. This native fold is the most stable state for that sequence.
Quaternary structure assembles several folded chains into one functional unit. Haemoglobin, with its four chains held by inter-subunit forces, is the classic example.

Here is the key contrast to carry forward. The primary level is covalent and tough, while levels two through four lean on weak bonds like hydrogen bonds. That difference is the whole story of denaturation.
Protein एक floppy string नहीं; यह structure के चार layered levels से fold होता है, हर एक पिछले पर बनता है।
यहाँ चारों sequence में हैं: bare chain, फिर local coils और sheets, फिर पूरा three-dimensional fold, फिर कई folded chains एक साथ assembled।
Primary structure बस amino acids का sequence है, covalent peptide bonds से जुड़ा। एक residue बदलो और protein की identity बदल जाती है।
Secondary structure पहला folding response है। Planar peptide units hydrogen-bond बनाकर regular patterns में बैठते हैं: coiled alpha-helix और folded beta-pleated sheet।
Alpha-helix में chain एक right-handed screw में मुड़ती है, और हर backbone carbonyl एक amine hydrogen से एक turn आगे hydrogen-bond बनाता है। Sheet में extended chains side by side bond करती हैं।
Tertiary structure उस secondary shape को एक compact three-dimensional form में pack करता है, या तो fibrous rod या globular ball। यह native fold उस sequence के लिए सबसे stable state है।
Quaternary structure कई folded chains को एक functional unit में assemble करता है। Haemoglobin, अपनी four chains के साथ inter-subunit forces से बँधी, classic example है।
यह key contrast आगे ले चलो। Primary level covalent और tough है, जबकि levels दो से चार hydrogen bonds जैसे weak bonds पर टिके हैं। यही difference denaturation की पूरी कहानी है।

board_events.text: Fibrous: parallel chains, insoluble, structural

A folded saree: the cloth is fixed, the folding makes it wearable
Boil it and it crumples: that is denaturation
Denaturation destroys secondary/tertiary/quaternary, spares primary
Usually irreversible: a boiled egg, milk curdled to paneer

segments.text: Tertiary folds come in two broad shapes, and understanding them makes denaturation fall into place immediately.
On the left, fibrous proteins; on the right, globular ones; and below, what heat or a pH change does to either of them.
Fibrous proteins have parallel chains arranged fibre-like, held by hydrogen and disulphide bonds. They are water-insoluble and structural: keratin in hair and wool, myosin, and collagen.
Globular proteins coil into a rough sphere, held mainly by hydrogen bonds. They are water-soluble and do the active jobs: insulin, albumin, and haemoglobin.
Picture a freshly ironed, perfectly folded saree. The cloth, the sequence, is fixed, but it is the folding that lets it be worn. Proteins are the same: the shape is what makes them useful.

Now throw that saree into boiling water and it crumples. The cloth is unchanged but the useful shape is gone. That crumpling is denaturation: heat or a pH change snaps the weak bonds and the protein unfolds.

Read denaturation precisely: it destroys the secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure and kills biological activity, but it leaves the primary covalent sequence completely intact. It does not break peptide bonds.
It is usually irreversible. A boiled egg white setting solid, or milk curdling into paneer, are denaturation you can watch in the kitchen. The proteins have unfolded, not been chopped up.
Tertiary folds दो broad shapes में आते हैं, और इन्हें समझ लेना denaturation को तुरंत साफ़ कर देता है।
बाईं ओर fibrous proteins; दाईं ओर globular; और नीचे, heat या pH change इन दोनों के साथ क्या करता है।
Fibrous proteins की parallel chains fibre-like arranged होती हैं, hydrogen और disulphide bonds से बँधी। ये water-insoluble और structural हैं: बालों और wool में keratin, myosin, और collagen।
Globular proteins एक rough sphere में coil होती हैं, मुख्यतः hydrogen bonds से बँधी। ये water-soluble हैं और active काम करती हैं: insulin, albumin, और haemoglobin।
एक ताज़ा इस्त्री की हुई, perfectly folded साड़ी सोचो। कपड़ा, यानी sequence, fixed है, पर folding ही उसे पहनने लायक़ बनाती है। Proteins वैसे ही हैं: shape ही उन्हें useful बनाती है।
अब उस साड़ी को उबलते पानी में डालो और वो सिकुड़ जाती है। कपड़ा वही है पर useful shape चली गई। वही सिकुड़ना denaturation है: heat या pH change weak bonds तोड़ता है और protein unfold हो जाता है।

Denaturation को precisely पढ़ो: यह secondary, tertiary और quaternary structure नष्ट करता है और biological activity ख़त्म करता है, पर primary covalent sequence को पूरी तरह intact छोड़ देता है। यह peptide bonds नहीं तोड़ता।
यह आम तौर पर irreversible है। उबले अंडे का सफ़ेद भाग ठोस होना, या दूध का पनीर में फटना, ऐसी denaturation है जो रसोई में देख सकते हो। Proteins unfold हुए हैं, कटे नहीं।

sections.title: The skeletons and the counting rules

board_events.text: The skeletons and the counting rules
D/L is configuration; the plus or minus sign is measured rotation

board_events.latex: -CO-NH- \;\; \text{peptide (amide) linkage, formed with loss of one } H_2O

board_events.text: About forty percent double-bond character keeps the amide flat
A restated toolkit; the full-chapter recap comes at the very end

segments.text: Proteins carry no dimensional formulae, so the toolkit here is the two skeletons, one caution, and a couple of counting rules. Here they are, restated for quick recall.

First the two skeletons. The general alpha-amino acid is R attached to a carbon bearing an amino group and a carboxyl. Its zwitter ion moves the proton, giving an ammonium cation and a carboxylate anion on the same molecule.

The standing caution: the D and L letters give configuration, compared with glyceraldehyde at the alpha-carbon, while the plus and minus sign is the measured direction of rotation. Natural amino acids are L, whatever their sign.
The peptide linkage itself is the amide group, formed by condensation with the loss of one water. It is the covalent bond that defines primary structure.

The chain rule, tested constantly: for n residues there are n minus one peptide bonds, and n minus one waters, released on assembly or consumed on hydrolysis. Students who write n instead of n minus one lose easy marks.

For sequence counting: with each of n distinct residues used once, there are n factorial orderings. If any of k residues may repeat across n positions, there are k to the power n. For a tripeptide that is three factorial, six, or three cubed, twenty seven.
Then remember the geometry number: the carbon-nitrogen link has about forty percent double-bond character, which keeps the amide unit planar and trans, with no free rotation across it.
Treat this as your protein toolkit, restated for reference rather than re-taught. The single consolidated formula recap for the whole chapter arrives at the very end of the final part.
Proteins के पास dimensional formulae नहीं, तो यहाँ toolkit है दो skeletons, एक caution, और कुछ counting rules। ये रहे, quick recall के लिए restated।

पहले दो skeletons। General alpha-amino acid है R जुड़ा एक carbon से जो amino group और carboxyl रखता है। इसका zwitter ion proton हटाता है, उसी molecule पर एक ammonium cation और एक carboxylate anion देकर।

Standing caution: D और L letters configuration देते हैं, alpha-carbon पर glyceraldehyde से compared, जबकि plus और minus sign rotation की measured direction है। Natural amino acids L हैं, उनका sign चाहे कुछ भी हो।
Peptide linkage खुद amide group है, condensation से एक water की loss के साथ बनी। यही covalent bond primary structure को define करता है।

Chain rule, लगातार tested: n residues के लिए n minus one peptide bonds होते हैं, और n minus one waters, assembly पर released या hydrolysis पर consumed। जो n minus one की जगह n लिखते हैं वो easy marks गँवाते हैं।

Sequence counting के लिए: n distinct residues हर एक बार use हों, तो n factorial orderings होते हैं। अगर k residues में से कोई n positions पर repeat हो सके, तो k की power n। एक tripeptide के लिए वो three factorial यानी six, या three cubed यानी twenty seven।
फिर geometry number याद रखो: carbon-nitrogen link लगभग forty percent double-bond character रखता है, जो amide unit को planar और trans रखता है, इसके across कोई free rotation नहीं।
इसे अपना protein toolkit समझो, reference के लिए restated, दोबारा पढ़ाया नहीं। पूरे chapter का single consolidated formula recap आख़िरी part के बिलकुल अंत में आता है।

Answer: zwitter-ion formation makes alanine salt-like and amphoteric

segments.text: A clean board question. Explain why alanine behaves like a salt rather than an ordinary amine or acid, and why it reacts with both hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide. Support it with the ionic forms.
Start from the structure. Alanine carries an acidic carboxyl group and a basic amino group on the same molecule, so it can react internally.
Here is the whole answer in one picture: the zwitter ion in the middle, its cation after adding acid on the left, and its anion after adding base on the right.
For part a, in water the carboxyl donates its proton to the amino group internally, producing the dipolar zwitter ion. The molecule now holds a full positive and a full negative charge.
Because it is now effectively an internal salt, alanine shows the high melting point and water solubility of ionic salts, not the volatility of a simple amine or acid. That answers part a.
For part b, add hydrochloric acid and the negative carboxylate end accepts a proton, turning alanine into a cation.
Add sodium hydroxide instead and the positive ammonium end loses a proton, turning alanine into an anion. It responds to both reagents.
So the full answer: the simultaneous presence of an acidic and a basic group, through zwitter-ion formation, makes alanine both salt-like and amphoteric. One idea settles the whole question.

एक clean board question। समझाओ कि alanine एक ordinary amine या acid के बजाय salt जैसा क्यों behave करता है, और यह hydrochloric acid और sodium hydroxide दोनों से क्यों react करता है। Ionic forms के साथ support करो।
Structure से शुरू करो। Alanine एक acidic carboxyl group और एक basic amino group एक ही molecule पर रखता है, तो यह अंदर ही react कर सकता है।
यह रहा पूरा answer एक picture में: बीच में zwitter ion, बाईं ओर acid डालने के बाद इसका cation, और दाईं ओर base डालने के बाद इसका anion।
Part a के लिए, पानी में carboxyl अपना proton अंदर ही amino group को देता है, dipolar zwitter ion बनाकर। Molecule अब एक पूरा positive और एक पूरा negative charge रखता है।
चूँकि यह अब effectively एक internal salt है, alanine ionic salts वाला high melting point और water solubility दिखाता है, न कि एक simple amine या acid की volatility। यह part a का जवाब है।
Part b के लिए, hydrochloric acid डालो और negative carboxylate end एक proton accept करता है, alanine को एक cation में बदलकर।
इसके बजाय sodium hydroxide डालो और positive ammonium end एक proton खोता है, alanine को एक anion में बदलकर। यह दोनों reagents को respond करता है।
तो पूरा answer: एक acidic और एक basic group का एक साथ होना, zwitter-ion formation के ज़रिए, alanine को salt-like और amphoteric दोनों बनाता है। एक idea पूरा सवाल settle कर देता है।

segments.text: A fast N E E T-style item. Classify each amino acid as acidic, basic or neutral by inspection: glutamic acid, lysine, and valine, given only their side chains.
The trap is rote recall. Students try to remember long lists and slip. The fast, reliable route is to count functional groups, ignoring the backbone's own single amino and single carboxyl.
Here is the comparison at a glance: only the extra groups inside R decide the class. Read across and the answer is immediate.
So read only the side chain. Whatever acidic or basic groups R adds, beyond the standard backbone, is what tips the balance.
Glutamic acid's side chain adds an extra carboxyl, so carboxyls now outnumber aminos. It is acidic.
Lysine's side chain adds an extra amino group, so aminos now outnumber carboxyls. It is basic.
Valine's side chain is a plain hydrocarbon with no extra acidic or basic group, so the counts stay equal. It is neutral.
So the answer is acidic, basic, and neutral, in that order. The shortcut collapses a memorised list into a two-second count: extra carboxyl acidic, extra amino basic, neither neutral.
एक तेज़ N E E T-style item। हर amino acid को inspection से acidic, basic या neutral classify करो: glutamic acid, lysine, और valine, सिर्फ उनके side chains दिए हुए।

Trap rote recall है। Students लंबी lists याद करने की कोशिश करते हैं और फिसल जाते हैं। तेज़, reliable route है functional groups गिनना, backbone के अपने single amino और single carboxyl को नज़रअंदाज़ करके।
यह रही comparison एक नज़र में: सिर्फ R के अंदर के extra groups class तय करते हैं। Across पढ़ो और answer तुरंत मिल जाता है।
तो सिर्फ side chain पढ़ो। R जो भी acidic या basic groups जोड़ता है, standard backbone से परे, वही संतुलन झुका देता है।
Glutamic acid के side chain में एक extra carboxyl है, तो अब carboxyls aminos से ज़्यादा हैं। यह acidic है।
Lysine के side chain में एक extra amino group है, तो अब aminos carboxyls से ज़्यादा हैं। यह basic है।
Valine का side chain एक plain hydrocarbon है, कोई extra acidic या basic group नहीं, तो counts बराबर रहते हैं। यह neutral है।
तो answer है acidic, basic, और neutral, इसी order में। Shortcut एक memorised list को two-second count में बदल देता है: extra carboxyl acidic, extra amino basic, कुछ नहीं तो neutral।

board_events.text: Part one: five residues give four peptide bonds
Part two: four bonds release four waters on assembly
